test_title: PYST 1: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: english
question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

The novel which had remained unpublished for decades (1)/ was discovered by chance in a locked drawer (2)/ and were later translated into multiple languages (3)/ by a well-known critic. (4)

options.text: The novel which had remained unpublished for decades (1)
was discovered by chance in a locked drawer (2)
and were later translated into multiple languages (3)

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error is in **part (3)** of the sentence due to a **subject-verb agreement** violation.
 
• The subject of the sentence is "**The novel**," which is a singular noun.
 
• In a sentence with a compound predicate (two or more actions for the same subject), all verbs must agree with that subject. While the first verb "was discovered" (part 2) correctly matches the singular subject, the second verb "**were**" (part 3) is plural.
 
• The plural verb "were" must be replaced with the singular verb "**was**" to maintain grammatical consistency.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The novel which had remained unpublished for decades was discovered by chance in a locked drawer and **was** later translated into multiple languages by a well-known critic."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1: "The novel which had remained..."** – This part is correct. The past perfect tense ("had remained") correctly indicates an action that was completed before another past action (the discovery).
 
• **2: "was discovered by chance..."** – This is the correct singular passive voice construction matching the subject "The novel."
 
• **4: "by a well-known critic"** – This part is correct. The compound adjective "well-known" is properly hyphenated before the noun it modifies.
 
• **Grammar Tip:** When a sentence is long or contains intervening phrases (like "which had remained unpublished for decades"), always trace the verb back to the **main subject** to ensure they agree in number.
